define.text: A storage appliance made of software: two virtual machines on one VMware host, working as one storage system.
One of the two virtual machines. On its own it is not the appliance; the two nodes mirror each other and share the work.
Management is how you reach the web page. Storage carries disk traffic. The interconnect is a private back channel between the two nodes.
A named door on a virtual switch. The name is a label, not a wall: two doors with the same network number open into the same room.
The network number that decides which room a door opens into. Untagged, VLAN zero, or a dash means the room with no number.
The private path the two nodes use to find each other during installation and to mirror data afterwards.

define.text: A separate port group name is a label, not a wall. Untagged groups on one switch are one room, however many names they have. The interconnect needs its own room.
Both nodes share a host today, so their traffic stays local. If VMware moves a node, the physical cables must carry those network numbers.
The appliance was never broken. The room was too crowded. Give the private link its own room, and the two halves can agree to become one.
